stemBlocks.value: The data matrix S = (12 9 5 / 15 7 8) shows the numbers of small, medium and large school shirts sold, with row 1 for Monday and row 2 for Tuesday. (a) How many medium shirts were sold on Tuesday? (b) Write a row matrix representing the total sales of each size over the two days. (c) Calculate the total number of shirts sold on Monday.
Think first: Rows are days and columns are sizes, so every question here is about picking the right row, the right column, or the right total.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p201-q15 from workbook page 201.

solutionSteps.instruction: Go to the Tuesday row and the medium column.

contentBlocks.value: Tuesday is row 2, medium is the middle column.

solutionSteps.instruction: Add the two rows column by column to combine the days.
Add all three entries of the Monday row.

strategyBlocks.value: Locate the Tuesday row and medium column for (a), add the two rows column by column for (b), and add across the Monday row for (c).

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) 7 medium shirts were sold on Tuesday  (b) The row matrix of two-day totals by size is (27 16 13)  (c) 26 shirts were sold on Monday in total.

whyThisWorks.value: A data matrix is a table with the labels stripped away, so meaning comes entirely from knowing what rows and columns stand for. Adding down a column combines the same size across days, while adding along a row combines all sizes within one day. Choosing the right direction is the whole skill.
